events.text: {op9_holder}, who keeps {op9_post}, will swear to {op9_seat} for a price, and says so across a pot of cold tea. It is a fair price, for the isles: one the Jade Court would call a courtesy. {op9_voice} says that {op9_n} others have already bowed, and that {op9_post} does not like to be the last.

choices.text: Pay the price, and have the oath

effects.log: The stones change hands and the oath is made. {op9_holder} looks, for a moment, almost fond of the transaction.

choices.text: Decline, and say the seat is not for sale

effects.log: You decline politely. {op9_post} stays its own master, which is what it wanted all along.

events.text: A cloud-barge delivers a bill: the keeper of {op9_post}, {op9_holder}, would like a tithe of stones before swearing to {op9_seat}. Not a bribe, the letter insists, but a retainer. It is written in a very small, very expensive hand, and the stamp is not that of the Ministry of Stores.

choices.text: Settle the retainer, and call it an oath

effects.log: The retainer goes by the next barge. A week later, so does the oath.

choices.text: Return the letter with a cup of plain tea

effects.log: The letter goes back with the tea. It is the one reply the keeper did not draft for.

events.text: {op9_holder} sends no word, only a ledger, open on the table of {op9_post}: the cost of lamp-oil, the cost of scribes, the cost of a roof that has leaked since the last Eclipse. The sum at the bottom is circled. {op9_voice} does not mention it. Everyone else does.

choices.text: Cover the sum, and take the oath that follows

effects.log: The roof is mended and the lamps lit. {op9_holder} swears with a hand on the new beam.

choices.text: Close the ledger, and offer a smaller kindness

effects.log: You offer a smaller kindness. It is accepted with a thin smile, and no oath.

events.text: {op9_holder} will not swear to {op9_seat} on word alone. In {op9_post}, they set out a blank scroll and ask you to tell it who you are, in a way the old scrolls will believe. {op9_n} others have tried. The room is very quiet, and a dozen disciples have found reasons to be on the stair.

choices.text: Speak to the scroll, and make it listen

ok.log: The scroll warms as you speak. {op9_holder} reads the finished page twice and bows.

fail.log: The scroll stays cold. You have said true things, and not the right way round.

choices.text: Decline the test, and say the seat does not need a witness

effects.log: You decline. The scroll rolls itself back up with a small, offended sound.

events.text: In the lowest court of {op9_post}, {op9_holder} lays out a puzzle that the house has kept for a thousand years: a map with a missing river. Whoever finds it, swears, the old keepers say. {op9_voice} lights the lamps, and the room smells of ink and old tea.

choices.text: Study the map, and find the river

ok.log: You find the river under a smudge no one noticed. {op9_holder} swears, with an expression of relief.

fail.log: The river will not be found. You lose an afternoon, and the keeper loses patience.

choices.text: Say you came for friends, not riddles

effects.log: You say it plainly. The map is rolled up again, and {op9_holder} laughs, once, shortly.

events.text: A test of arms is the keeper's way, and {op9_holder} has chosen the courtyard of {op9_post} for it. No blades, only the hands and the old forms. Behind them {op9_voice} counts a breath for each of the isles the house has outlived. Win, and the oath is yours.

choices.text: Meet the keeper in the courtyard

ok.log: You win with a form from three centuries ago that {op9_holder} had thought lost. The oath is given on the spot.

fail.log: The keeper is better than the rumours. You walk out with a bruised arm and a polite word.

choices.text: Bow, and say there are no friends to be made by force

effects.log: You bow. {op9_holder} bows back, in a way that is neither agreement nor offence.

events.text: {op9_holder} asks no stones and sets no test. They ask for a promise, spoken in {op9_post}, to be kept at a time they will name later. {op9_voice} gives you a cup of plum wine, and says that it is a very old kind of oath, and a very dull one. {op9_n} have given it already.

choices.text: Give the promise, and raise the cup to it

effects.log: You give it, and raise the cup, and set it down full. Somewhere in the walls of {op9_post}, an old bell is struck once.

choices.text: Say you do not promise what you cannot yet see

effects.log: You say so, kindly. {op9_holder} writes something down, and does not say what.

events.text: The keeper of {op9_post} puts a folded paper on the table without a word. It says that when the day comes, you will do one thing, and it does not say what. The ink is ordinary, the paper is old, and {op9_voice} cannot quite look at it.

choices.text: Sign the paper without reading it twice

effects.log: You sign. The paper is folded, and put in a drawer, and the drawer is locked with a small satisfied click.

choices.text: Fold the paper back, and say you would rather know

effects.log: You fold it back. {op9_holder} takes it, smiles faintly, and puts it away unsigned.

events.text: On the stair of {op9_post}, {op9_holder} stops you with one hand on the rail. A promise, they say, between friends of the seat: that when the isles are in trouble, you will come. No terms. No witness but the clouds. It is, as these things go, a very generous kind of rope.

choices.text: Promise, and mean it

effects.log: You promise. The clouds are the only witnesses, and they are, as always, discreet.

choices.text: Say you will come when you can, and no promise more

effects.log: You say so. {op9_holder} accepts it, thoughtfully, as one accepts a smaller coin.

events.text: The promise made in {op9_post} falls due. {op9_holder} does not send a messenger; they come themselves, in plain robes, on the last cloud-barge of the season. The thing they ask is smaller than you feared and harder than you hoped. {op9_voice} waits at the landing, pretending not to listen.

choices.text: Keep the promise, whatever it costs

effects.log: You keep it. {op9_holder} bows lower than the occasion needs.

choices.text: Break it, and send the keeper away

effects.log: You break it. The barge leaves with a single passenger, and the post of {op9_post} stays silent for years.

events.text: A letter in an old hand, delivered to your door by a child of {op9_post}: it is time. The thing you promised is no longer abstract, and it has a date, a place on the White Stairs, and a witness. {op9_holder} has underlined the date twice. You could keep it. You could also find a very good reason not to.

choices.text: Go to the White Stairs on the date

effects.log: You are on the stair at dawn. {op9_holder} is there too, and neither of you mentions how long you waited.

choices.text: Find a very good reason not to go

effects.log: The reason is very good. It is, nevertheless, a reason, and everyone in {op9_post} knows its shape.

events.text: The bell of {op9_post} rings three times at dusk, which only happens when a promise is called in. {op9_holder} stands at the door with {op9_voice}. Nobody speaks of the oath. They speak of the weather, and the price of lamp-oil, and when the tea is done, they simply look at you.

choices.text: Rise, and say that you remember

effects.log: You rise and say it. The bell rings once more, softly, and the oath is closed.

choices.text: Pour more tea, and say nothing at all

effects.log: You pour more tea. The silence is an answer, and nobody drinks.

events.text: Your heir {npc} has been to {op9_post}. The keeper, {op9_holder}, was offered a great gift of stones and seals in return for a different oath, one sworn to {npc}'s side of the quarrel. {op9_voice} found out and told you, in the tone of one reading a weather report. It is not yet too late to outbid.

choices.text: Match the offer, and keep the oath

effects.log: You match it. {op9_holder} accepts the stones, and the oath, with an air of mild regret at the haggling.

choices.text: Let {npc} have it, and save your stones

effects.log: You let it go. {npc} has bought a post in the house of {op9_seat}, and the house will remember who sold it.

events.text: A cloud-barge flying {npc}'s colours lands at {op9_post} by night. By morning {op9_holder} has a new robe, a new lamp, and a quiet look. {op9_voice} says that the keeper has been offered another oath, and that the price was very high. What is yours?

choices.text: Make a counter-offer before the barge leaves

effects.log: You make one. The barge leaves empty-handed, and {npc} is displeased.

choices.text: Wish the keeper well, and let the barge be

effects.log: You let it be. The oath goes to {npc}, with a bow and a receipt.

choices.text: Make a counter-offer before the barge leaves

effects.log: You make one. The barge leaves empty-handed, and {npc} is displeased.

choices.text: Wish the keeper well, and let the barge be

effects.log: You let it be. The oath goes to {npc}, with a bow and a receipt.

events.text: {npc} has made a move you did not expect: a gift, in your name, to the keeper of {op9_post}, which was never yours to give. It is a trap and a kindness at the same time. {op9_holder} cannot accept it without owing {npc}, and cannot refuse it without offending you.

choices.text: Cover the gift, and make it truly yours

effects.log: You cover it, and the gift becomes your own. {op9_holder} holds to the oath, with a small, grim smile.

choices.text: Let the gift stand, and let the debt fall where it falls

effects.log: You let it stand. The keeper owes {npc} now, and you owe the keeper an apology.

events.text: {npc} has made a move you did not expect: a gift, in your name, to the keeper of {op9_post}, which was never yours to give. It is a trap and a kindness at the same time. {op9_holder} cannot accept it without owing {npc}, and cannot refuse it without offending you.

choices.text: Cover the gift, and make it truly yours

effects.log: You cover it, and the gift becomes your own. {op9_holder} holds to the oath, with a small, grim smile.

choices.text: Let the gift stand, and let the debt fall where it falls

effects.log: You let it stand. The keeper owes {npc} now, and you owe the keeper an apology.

events.text: All four posts of {op9_seat} stand sworn to you at last. Every keeper of the house answers to one name. {op9_voice} stands at the head of the stair with the four keepers, who look, for once, like four of the same family. It is a quiet, rare, slightly alarming sight.

choices.text: Thank them, one at a time, by name

effects.log: You thank them by name. Four old heads bow. {op9_voice} wipes an eye with a sleeve.

choices.text: Say nothing, and lead them in to supper

effects.log: You lead them in. The soup is excellent, and nothing at all is signed.

events.text: The four keepers of {op9_seat} come to the same room on the same day, which has not happened in living memory. They do not speak of the oaths. They sit, and one of them pours the tea. It is, you realise, a kind of peace, and the first time the house has held one.

choices.text: Pour the next cup yourself

effects.log: You pour. It is a small gesture. It is received as a large one.

choices.text: Ask each of them for one honest complaint

effects.log: You ask. It takes the afternoon, and by the end the house is better for it.

events.text: {ow9_old} is gone, and named nobody. The seat of {ow9_seat} stands empty under its lamp, and {ow9_order} holds its breath. By evening a letter comes from {ow9_foe}, perfectly courteous, announcing a claim. The Jade Court has heard already, and is, in its fashion, delighted.

choices.text: Put your own claim to the Rolls

effects.log: You put it to the Rolls. The clerk writes it down without a flicker, which is a sign of good upbringing.

choices.text: Back {ow9_foe}, and kneel first

effects.log: You kneel first. {ow9_foe} is startled, and then gracious, and then rather quick.

choices.text: Step aside, and let the quarrel pass

effects.log: You step aside, and watch the quarrel go by like a barge in a fog.

events.text: The lamp of {ow9_seat} burns on, though {ow9_old} will never trim it again. In the courtyard of {ow9_order}, factions gather in knots. {ow9_foe} is the only one who has sent for a banner. They say the banner is already stitched, which is the sort of thing one says of a banner that is not.

choices.text: Take the lamp, and sit under it

effects.log: You take the lamp, and sit. The knots in the courtyard turn, slowly, to watch.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} your arm, and your name

effects.log: You offer both. It is taken, with a look of cautious happiness.

choices.text: Blow out the lamp, and go home

effects.log: You blow it out and go home. The courtyard, the next morning, is full of other people's smoke.

events.text: No will was found. {ow9_old} left tea, a pair of worn sandals and a seat of {ow9_seat} with a hundred hands reaching for it. {ow9_foe} is first among them, with a letter and a great deal of confidence. The elders of {ow9_order} look at you, one by one, and wait.

choices.text: Say you will hold the seat, and that you do not ask leave

effects.log: You say it. Several elders discover a pressing need to be elsewhere.

choices.text: Say you will follow {ow9_foe}, with conditions

effects.log: You follow, with conditions. They are written down, and some are even kept.

choices.text: Say the seat is not yours to want

effects.log: You say so. It is the truth, or nearly, and the elders hear it as modesty.

events.text: The war for {ow9_seat} is mostly teacups. In the east cloister, the gardeners of {ow9_order} have not yet declared; in the west, the scribes have. {ow9_foe} dines with the scribes every night. A voice is a thing you can win honestly, buy handsomely, or lean on until it speaks. Tonight it is the gardeners.

choices.text: Walk the east cloister, and ask for each voice

effects.log: You walk, and ask. Most of them say yes, in the way people say yes to a polite person.

choices.text: Send the gardeners the finest of your stores

effects.log: The gifts go out. The gardeners are moved, as gardeners are, by something that grows.

choices.text: Remind the gardeners who holds their leases

effects.log: You remind them. The gardeners promise, very quietly, and remember.

events.text: A cloud-barge full of ministers from the Court of Ascents sits off the isle of {ow9_order}, waiting to see who rules {ow9_seat}. They are not partial. They are merely curious, which is worse. {ow9_foe} has already invited them to dinner. The question is who invites them to breakfast.

choices.text: Invite them to breakfast, and tell them the plain truth

effects.log: You tell them. The ministers eat well and write nothing down, which is a compliment.

choices.text: Send a hamper of the isle's best, with no note

effects.log: The hamper goes aboard. The barge, in its slow way, begins to turn.

choices.text: Mention a few things the Court would rather not hear

effects.log: You mention them. The barge is suddenly eager to be on its way.

events.text: The old disciples of {ow9_old} are the swing. Eleven of them live on the high terrace, and each has a vote worth three. They loved their master in different ways, which is the trouble. {ow9_foe} has promised them a monument. You could promise them a better one, or something else.

choices.text: Sit with each of them, and speak of {ow9_old}

effects.log: You sit with each, and speak. The disciples remember who came to listen.

choices.text: Promise a monument, and pay for the first stone

effects.log: The first stone is laid. The disciples begin, in a noticeable way, to like you.

choices.text: Hint that the monument will not be built at all

effects.log: You hint. They go quiet, and nod, and do not meet your eye.

events.text: Under the lantern-trees of {ow9_order}, a ring of senior immortals sip wine and weigh the claims. They want to be wooed, and they want not to be seen wooed. {ow9_foe} has failed at both. It is your turn, and the senior immortal with the longest beard is already smiling.

choices.text: Speak to them straight, without the wine

effects.log: You speak straight. Two of the old ones nod, slowly, like a pair of herons.

choices.text: Lay out a feast the isles will talk about

effects.log: The feast is talked about. The senior immortals are in a mood to be generous.

choices.text: Let them know what an open quarrel will cost them

effects.log: You let them know. They take it as a statement of fact, which it is.

events.text: A skirmish breaks out in the Hall of the Long Table, between the guard loyal to you and the guard loyal to {ow9_foe}. Nothing is drawn but tempers, and a chair goes through a screen of painted cranes. The elders of {ow9_order} watch from the gallery, and every word you say now will be repeated at supper.

choices.text: Step between them and speak to both

ok.log: You step between them and speak. The skirmish drains away, and the elders are impressed.

fail.log: You step between them and speak, and are shouted over. The elders watch your face colour.

choices.text: Let them fight, and talk to the elders instead

effects.log: You turn your back on the fray and speak to the gallery. It is a calm, risky thing to do, and it works.

events.text: The great gate of {ow9_order} is shut by one party and opened by another, three times in one morning. A bell is rung wrongly. A banner of {ow9_foe}'s is pinned over a banner of yours. The Hall of Records is next, and whoever holds the Records, holds the argument. You have maybe ten breaths.

choices.text: Find the clause in the Records that settles it

ok.log: You find the clause, a tiny line in an old charter, and read it aloud. The hall falls quiet.

fail.log: You hunt for the clause, and the clause is not where you hoped. The hall's mood is not improved.

choices.text: Stand in the gate and hold it with your name

effects.log: You stand in the gate. Your name does the rest, and the bell is rung rightly.

events.text: Ranks of lanterns are carried through the halls of {ow9_order}, each side trying to out-light the other. It is a ridiculous war and a serious one. In the Chamber of Seals, a candle has been knocked over, and a cabinet of old seals is smoking. {ow9_foe} is nowhere. The seals are everywhere.

choices.text: Take command of the room, and organise the buckets

ok.log: You organise the buckets. By the time the smoke clears, the whole hall is quietly on your side.

fail.log: You shout for buckets and nobody comes. The seals are saved by a very small cook.

choices.text: Save the seals yourself, and say nothing about it

effects.log: You save the seals yourself, quietly. The scribes see it, and the scribes remember.

events.text: The matter comes down to a duel on the Terrace of Mist, as these matters do. {ow9_foe} waits at the far end, in their best robe. The white stones of {ow9_seat} are watching. Your side is thin, and the elders say little. It is going to be close, and it is going to be seen from every isle.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} on the Terrace

effects.log: You meet them. The mist closes round the two of you, and what follows is not for the record.

choices.text: Step aside before it begins

effects.log: You step aside. {ow9_foe} is given the seat, and the Terrace is swept.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sends a challenge, written on rice paper, folded into a crane. The crane is placed on your desk by a child of {ow9_order} who is visibly terrified. The terms: a single bout, no seconds, at dawn, for {ow9_seat}. You have fewer friends than you would like.

choices.text: Fold the crane back, and accept

effects.log: You accept. The crane flies home, and the isle does not sleep that night.

choices.text: Burn the crane, and concede the seat

effects.log: You burn it, and concede. The smoke goes up in a thin and very polite line.

events.text: The elders have decided that the seat of {ow9_order} goes to the winner of a duel, which is to say they have decided not to decide. {ow9_foe} has trained for a year. You were busy. The White Stairs are lined, as for a festival, with people who have pinned a little hope on you.

choices.text: Go up the stairs, and meet them

effects.log: You go up. The crowd parts, and the duel begins in a silence like a held breath.

choices.text: Decline, and watch from the second step

effects.log: You decline. The second step is, you find, a very good place to watch the future go by.

events.text: The elders of {ow9_order} have rallied to you, one by one, and now {ow9_foe} stands alone in the courtyard, with a sword and a very straight back. It would end quickly. It would also be remembered. The isles look on, hushed, hoping for a clean ending.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} in the open, and finish it

effects.log: You meet them. The courtyard watches, and it is quick, and it is cleanly done.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} a hall and a place at your table

effects.log: You offer terms. {ow9_foe} takes a long time to say yes, and then says it well.

events.text: With the voices behind you, the matter of {ow9_seat} is nearly settled. {ow9_foe} sends a last message: a duel, if you like, or terms, if you are wise. The hall of {ow9_order} is lit for either. Someone has already laid out a seat, a sword, and a pot of tea.

choices.text: Take the duel, and be done

effects.log: You take it. The sword is lighter than you thought, and the ending cleaner.

choices.text: Take the tea, and write the terms

effects.log: You take the tea, and write the terms. They are generous, and fair.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_seat} is yours. {ow9_old}'s lamp still burns beside it, and the first thing you do is trim it. The isle of {ow9_order} has begun to say your name in the tone of a house that has decided. In the corner, a very old cook weeps into a very large pot.

choices.text: Keep {ow9_old}'s sandals by the seat

effects.log: You keep them. The house is quietly glad.

choices.text: Give the seat's first feast to the whole isle

effects.log: You give the feast. Every table is full, and the lanterns burn until dawn.

events.text: You sit in {ow9_seat} for the first time, and it is, as every seat is, a little too hard. {ow9_old} would have told you that. The elders of {ow9_order} bow in order, the youngest last. Outside, the White Stairs are swept and a hundred cloud-barges are lifting off with the news.

choices.text: Rise, and walk the isle before nightfall

effects.log: You walk it. The disciples line the path, and the old stones are warm under your feet.

choices.text: Send a letter to {ow9_foe}, and invite them to supper

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} comes, and the supper is awkward and honest.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sits in {ow9_seat}, and you stand in the second row. It is not a disgrace, but it is a position. {ow9_old} would have said something wise. You say nothing, and bow when the others bow. The tea afterward is unusually good.

choices.text: Bow deeply, and mean none of it yet

effects.log: You bow. Meaning will come, or it will not.

choices.text: Write your faults down, in a plain hand

effects.log: You write them. The list is shorter than you feared, and sharper.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_order} is {ow9_foe}'s, and the isle breathes out. You are left with your sword, your stones, and a long list of people who no longer meet your eye. The Terrace of Mist is swept clean. A single crane lands on the rail, looks at you, and leaves.

choices.text: Walk the isle at night, alone

effects.log: You walk it. The stones are cool, and you learn the names of the lamps.

choices.text: Send {ow9_foe} a gift, and a short, honest note

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} sends back a gift of tea, which is a start.

events.text: {op9_holder}, who keeps {op9_post}, will pledge to {op9_seat} in return for an offering, and says so in the cold hours between two prayers. The offering is a fair one, for a god. {op9_voice} adds that {op9_n} others have already knelt, and that {op9_post} does not like to be the last in the Book.

choices.text: Make the offering, and have the oath

effects.log: The offering is accepted, with a glow of faith, and the oath follows like a small, warm bell.

choices.text: Decline, and say the domain is not for sale

effects.log: You decline. {op9_post} stays its own, which is exactly the answer it was fishing for.

events.text: A herald arrives with a bill in letters of gold-leaf: {op9_holder} asks a tithe of faith before pledging to {op9_seat}. Not a bribe, the herald stresses, but a gift of continuance. The seal is the wrong seal, and the herald knows it, and looks past your shoulder.

choices.text: Pay the tithe, and call it a gift

effects.log: The tithe goes up the star-road. The oath comes down it a day later, tidy as a cut flower.

choices.text: Return the bill with a flower from your own altar

effects.log: You send a flower. The herald takes it back with an air of unwilling admiration.

events.text: {op9_holder} sends no message, only an account: the cost of incense, of chanting, of a roof of stars that leaks. The sum at the bottom is circled. {op9_voice} does not mention it. The silence in {op9_post} does.

choices.text: Cover the cost, and hear the oath

effects.log: You cover the cost. The roof of stars mends itself, and the oath is given in a high, clear voice.

choices.text: Offer a smaller blessing instead

effects.log: You offer a smaller blessing. It is accepted with a thin smile, and no oath.

events.text: {op9_holder} will not pledge to {op9_seat} on word alone. In {op9_post}, they set out an empty bowl and ask you to fill it with a prayer that is yours alone. {op9_n} have tried. The room is very quiet, and the incense has stopped moving.

choices.text: Pray into the bowl, and let it fill

ok.log: The bowl fills with light. {op9_holder} lifts it, tastes it, and bows.

fail.log: The bowl stays dry. The words were true, and not yours enough.

choices.text: Decline the test, and say a god needs no witness

effects.log: You decline. The bowl is turned over with a small sound of reproach.

events.text: In the inner shrine of {op9_post}, {op9_holder} sets a riddle that the house has kept for an age: a page of the Book of Fates with a missing name. Whoever finds it, pledges, say the old heralds. {op9_voice} lights the lamps, and the air smells of ink and rain on stone.

choices.text: Study the page, and find the name

ok.log: You find the name, under a smear no one else saw. {op9_holder} pledges, with a sigh of relief.

fail.log: The name stays hidden. You lose an evening, and {op9_holder} loses patience.

choices.text: Say you came for allies, not riddles

effects.log: You say it plainly. The page is closed, and {op9_holder} laughs, once.

events.text: The keeper of {op9_post} proposes a trial of might. No weapons, only the god-hands and the old forms, in the cloister below. {op9_voice} counts the stars of the domain, one for each breath. Win, and the pledge is given.

choices.text: Meet the keeper in the cloister

ok.log: You win with a hold from the first age that {op9_holder} had thought lost. The pledge is given on the spot.

fail.log: The keeper is better than the rumours. You leave with a bruised arm and a courteous word.

choices.text: Bow, and say allies are not won by force

effects.log: You bow. {op9_holder} bows back, in a way that is neither agreement nor offence.

events.text: {op9_holder} asks no offering and sets no trial, only a promise spoken in {op9_post}, to be called in when they choose. {op9_voice} brings a cup of star-wine and says it is a very old kind of oath, and a very dull one. {op9_n} have sworn it already.

choices.text: Give the promise, and raise the cup to it

effects.log: You give it, and raise the cup, and set it down full. Somewhere in {op9_post}, an old chime sounds once.

choices.text: Say you do not promise what you cannot yet see

effects.log: You say so, kindly. {op9_holder} makes a note in the margin of the Book.

events.text: The keeper of {op9_post} lays a folded leaf on the altar. It says that when the day comes you will do one thing, and does not say what. The leaf is ordinary, the ink is old, and {op9_voice} cannot quite look at it.

choices.text: Sign the leaf without reading it twice

effects.log: You sign. The leaf is folded, and put away, and the shrine gives a small satisfied sigh.

choices.text: Fold the leaf back, and say you would rather know

effects.log: You fold it back. {op9_holder} takes it, smiles faintly, and puts it away unsigned.

events.text: On the star-road outside {op9_post}, {op9_holder} stops you with one hand on the cold rail. A promise, they say, between friends of the domain: that when the pantheon is in trouble, you will come. No terms, no witness but the stars. It is a very generous kind of rope.

choices.text: Promise, and mean it

effects.log: You promise. The stars are the only witnesses, and they are discreet.

choices.text: Say you will come when you can, and promise no more

effects.log: You say so. {op9_holder} accepts it, thoughtfully, as one accepts a smaller coin.

events.text: The promise made in {op9_post} falls due. {op9_holder} sends no herald; they come themselves, in a plain mantle, on the last star-road of the season. The thing they ask is smaller than you feared and harder than you hoped. {op9_voice} waits at the gate, pretending not to listen.

choices.text: Keep the promise, whatever it costs

effects.log: You keep it. {op9_holder} bows lower than the occasion needs.

choices.text: Break it, and send the keeper away

effects.log: You break it. The star-road is quiet, and the post of {op9_post} stays dark for an age.

events.text: A letter of light, delivered to your altar by an acolyte of {op9_post}: it is time. The thing you promised is no longer abstract, and has a date, a place on the road of stars, and a witness. {op9_holder} has underlined the date twice. You could keep it. You could find a splendid reason not to.

choices.text: Go to the road of stars on the date

effects.log: You are on the road at dusk. {op9_holder} is there too, and neither of you mentions how long you waited.

choices.text: Find a splendid reason not to go

effects.log: The reason is splendid. It is, nevertheless, a reason, and everyone in {op9_post} knows its shape.

events.text: The chime of {op9_post} rings three times at the turning of the watch, which only happens when a promise is called in. {op9_holder} stands at the door with {op9_voice}. Nobody speaks of the oath. They speak of faith, and the weather above the clouds, and when the wine is done, they look at you.

choices.text: Rise, and say that you remember

effects.log: You rise and say it. The chime sounds once more, softly, and the oath is closed.

choices.text: Refill the cups, and say nothing

effects.log: You refill the cups. The silence is an answer, and nobody drinks.

events.text: Your heir {npc} has been to {op9_post}. The keeper, {op9_holder}, was offered a great flow of faith in return for a different pledge, one made to {npc}'s side of the quarrel. {op9_voice} found out and told you, in the tone of one reading a weather report. It is not yet too late to outbid.

choices.text: Match the offer, and keep the pledge

effects.log: You match it. {op9_holder} accepts the faith, and the pledge, with a trace of regret at the haggling.

choices.text: Let {npc} have it, and keep your faith

effects.log: You let it go. {npc} has bought a post in {op9_seat}, and the domain will remember who sold it.

choices.text: Let {npc} have it, and keep your faith

effects.log: You let it go. {npc} has bought a post in {op9_seat}, and the domain will remember who sold it.

events.text: A star-road lights up with {npc}'s colours and ends at the gate of {op9_post}. By morning {op9_holder} has a new mantle, a new censer, and a quiet look. {op9_voice} says the keeper has been offered another pledge, and the price was very high. What is yours?

choices.text: Make a counter-offer before the road goes dark

effects.log: You make one. The road goes dark with nothing carried, and {npc} is displeased.

choices.text: Wish the keeper well, and let the road be

effects.log: You let it be. The pledge goes to {npc}, with a bow and a seal.

events.text: A star-road lights up with {npc}'s colours and ends at the gate of {op9_post}. By morning {op9_holder} has a new mantle, a new censer, and a quiet look. {op9_voice} says the keeper has been offered another pledge, and the price was very high. What is yours?

choices.text: Make a counter-offer before the road goes dark

effects.log: You make one. The road goes dark with nothing carried, and {npc} is displeased.

choices.text: Wish the keeper well, and let the road be

effects.log: You let it be. The pledge goes to {npc}, with a bow and a seal.

events.text: {npc} has made a move you did not expect: a gift, in your name, to the keeper of {op9_post}, which was never yours to give. It is a trap and a kindness at once. {op9_holder} cannot accept it without owing {npc}, and cannot refuse it without offending you.

choices.text: Cover the gift, and make it truly yours

effects.log: You cover it, and the gift becomes your own. {op9_holder} holds to the pledge, with a small, grim smile.

choices.text: Let the gift stand, and let the debt fall where it falls

effects.log: You let it stand. The keeper owes {npc} now, and you owe the keeper an apology.

events.text: {npc} has made a move you did not expect: a gift, in your name, to the keeper of {op9_post}, which was never yours to give. It is a trap and a kindness at once. {op9_holder} cannot accept it without owing {npc}, and cannot refuse it without offending you.

choices.text: Cover the gift, and make it truly yours

effects.log: You cover it, and the gift becomes your own. {op9_holder} holds to the pledge, with a small, grim smile.

choices.text: Let the gift stand, and let the debt fall where it falls

effects.log: You let it stand. The keeper owes {npc} now, and you owe the keeper an apology.

events.text: All four posts of {op9_seat} stand pledged to you at last. Every keeper of the domain answers to one name. {op9_voice} stands at the head of the stair with the four keepers, who look, for once, like four of the same pantheon.

choices.text: Thank them, one at a time, by name

effects.log: You thank them by name. Four old heads bow. {op9_voice} wipes an eye with a sleeve.

choices.text: Say nothing, and lead them in to the offering feast

effects.log: You lead them in. The feast is long, and nothing at all is signed.

events.text: The four keepers of {op9_seat} come to the same chamber on the same day, which has not happened since the last Age. They do not speak of the pledges. They sit, and one of them pours the wine. It is, you realise, a kind of peace, and the first the domain has held.

choices.text: Pour the next cup yourself

effects.log: You pour. It is a small gesture, received as a large one.

choices.text: Ask each of them for one honest complaint

effects.log: You ask. It takes the evening, and by the end the domain is better for it.

events.text: {ow9_old} is gone, and named no heir. The seat of {ow9_seat} stands empty under its lamp of stars, and {ow9_order} holds its breath. By dusk a hymn of announcement comes from {ow9_foe}: a claim, perfectly courteous. The Book of Fates has already turned a page, and is, in its fashion, delighted.

choices.text: Put your own claim to the Book

effects.log: You put it to the Book. The page turns, and the ink takes a moment to decide.

choices.text: Back {ow9_foe}, and kneel first

effects.log: You kneel first. {ow9_foe} is startled, then gracious, then rather quick.

choices.text: Step aside, and let the quarrel pass

effects.log: You step aside, and watch the quarrel go by like a comet.

events.text: The lamp of {ow9_seat} burns on, though {ow9_old} will never trim it again. In the cloisters of {ow9_order}, gods gather in knots. {ow9_foe} is the only one who has sent for a standard. They say it is already woven, the way one says of a standard that is not.

choices.text: Take the lamp, and sit beneath it

effects.log: You take the lamp and sit. The knots in the cloister turn, slowly, to watch.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} your altar, and your name

effects.log: You offer both. It is taken, with a look of cautious happiness.

choices.text: Snuff the lamp, and go home

effects.log: You snuff it and go home. The cloister, the next morning, is full of other gods' smoke.

events.text: No testament was found. {ow9_old} left a cup, a worn mantle, and a seat of {ow9_seat} with a hundred hands reaching for it. {ow9_foe} is first among them, with a hymn and a great deal of confidence. The elder gods of {ow9_order} look at you, one by one, and wait.

choices.text: Say you will hold the seat, and need no leave

effects.log: You say it. Several elder gods discover pressing business on other star-roads.

choices.text: Say you will follow {ow9_foe}, with conditions

effects.log: You follow, with conditions. They are written in the Book, and some are even kept.

choices.text: Say the seat is not yours to want

effects.log: You say so. It is the truth, or nearly, and the elders hear it as humility.

events.text: The war for {ow9_seat} is waged mostly in prayers. In the east nave of {ow9_order}, the choir has not yet declared; in the west, the scribes have. {ow9_foe} dines with the scribes. A voice can be won honestly, bought handsomely, or leaned on. Tonight it is the choir.

choices.text: Walk the east nave, and ask for each voice

effects.log: You walk, and ask. Most of them say yes, as people say yes to the polite.

choices.text: Send the choir the finest offerings you have

effects.log: The offerings go out. The choir is moved, as choirs are, by incense and candles.

choices.text: Remind the choir who tends their altar

effects.log: You remind them. The choir promises, very quietly, and remembers.

events.text: A fleet of heralds from rival pantheons floats off the shrine of {ow9_order}, waiting to see who rules {ow9_seat}. They are not partial. They are merely curious, which is worse. {ow9_foe} has already invited them to a feast. The question is who invites them to the dawn rite.

choices.text: Invite them to the dawn rite, and tell the plain truth

effects.log: You tell them. The heralds eat nothing and write nothing, which is a compliment.

choices.text: Send a basket of first-fruits, unsigned

effects.log: The basket goes aboard. The fleet, in its slow way, begins to turn.

choices.text: Mention a few things their gods would rather not hear

effects.log: You mention them. The fleet is suddenly eager to be on its way.

events.text: The old acolytes of {ow9_old} are the swing. Eleven of them live in the high cloister, and each has a vote worth three. They loved their god in different ways, which is the trouble. {ow9_foe} has promised them a statue. You could promise a better one, or something else.

choices.text: Sit with each of them, and speak of {ow9_old}

effects.log: You sit with each, and speak. The acolytes remember who came to listen.

choices.text: Promise a statue, and pay for the first stone

effects.log: The first stone is laid. The acolytes begin, noticeably, to like you.

choices.text: Hint that the statue will never be raised at all

effects.log: You hint. They go quiet, and nod, and do not meet your eye.

events.text: Beneath the cedar-lamps of {ow9_order}, a ring of elder gods sip star-wine and weigh the claims. They want to be wooed, and not seen to be. {ow9_foe} has failed at both. It is your turn, and the god with the longest beard is already smiling.

choices.text: Speak to them plainly, without the wine

effects.log: You speak plainly. Two of the old gods nod, slowly, like a pair of herons.

choices.text: Lay out an offering the pantheon will talk about

effects.log: The offering is talked about. The elder gods are in a mood to be generous.

choices.text: Let them know what an open quarrel will cost them in faith

effects.log: You let them know. They take it as a statement of fact, which it is.

events.text: A skirmish breaks out in the Hall of Hours, between the heralds loyal to you and those loyal to {ow9_foe}. Nothing is drawn but tempers, and a censer goes through a screen of painted stars. The elders of {ow9_order} watch from the gallery, and every word you say will be repeated at the evening rite.

choices.text: Step between them and speak to both

ok.log: You step between them and speak. The skirmish drains away, and the elders are impressed.

fail.log: You step between them and speak, and are shouted down. The elders watch your halo flicker.

choices.text: Let them squabble, and speak to the elders instead

effects.log: You turn your back on the fray and speak to the gallery. It is a calm, risky thing to do, and it works.

events.text: The great gate of {ow9_order} is shut by one party and opened by another, three times in one morning. A bell is rung wrongly. A standard of {ow9_foe}'s is hung over one of yours. The Archive of Names is next, and whoever holds the Archive, holds the argument. You have maybe ten breaths.

choices.text: Find the clause in the Archive that settles it

ok.log: You find the clause, a tiny line in an old covenant, and read it aloud. The hall falls quiet.

fail.log: You hunt for the clause, and the clause is not where you hoped. The hall's mood is not improved.

choices.text: Stand in the gate and hold it with your name

effects.log: You stand in the gate. Your name does the rest, and the bell is rung rightly.

events.text: Rows of lamps are carried through the halls of {ow9_order}, each side trying to out-shine the other. It is a ridiculous war and a serious one. In the Chamber of Seals, a lamp has been knocked over, and a cabinet of sacred seals is smoking. {ow9_foe} is nowhere. The seals are everywhere.

choices.text: Take command of the room, and organise the water

ok.log: You organise the water. By the time the smoke clears, the whole hall is quietly on your side.

fail.log: You shout for water and nobody comes. The seals are saved by a very small acolyte.

choices.text: Save the seals yourself, and say nothing about it

effects.log: You save the seals yourself, quietly. The scribes see it, and the scribes remember.

events.text: The matter comes down to a duel on the Terrace of Dawn, as these matters do. {ow9_foe} waits at the far end, in their best mantle. The white stones of {ow9_seat} are watching. Your side is thin, and the elder gods say little. It will be close, and every shrine will see it.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} on the Terrace

effects.log: You meet them. The dawn closes round the two of you, and what follows is not for the Book.

choices.text: Step aside before it begins

effects.log: You step aside. {ow9_foe} is given the seat, and the Terrace is swept.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sends a challenge, written in light, folded into a dove. The dove lands on your altar and is carried in by an acolyte of {ow9_order} who is visibly terrified. The terms: a single bout, no seconds, at the hour of dawn, for {ow9_seat}. You have fewer worshippers than you would like.

choices.text: Send the dove back, and accept

effects.log: You accept. The dove flies home, and the pantheon does not sleep that night.

choices.text: Let the dove burn out, and concede the seat

effects.log: You let it burn out, and concede. The light goes up in a thin and very polite line.

events.text: The elder gods have decided that the seat of {ow9_order} goes to the winner of a duel, which is to say they have decided not to decide. {ow9_foe} has trained for an age. You were busy. The star-road is lined, as for a festival, with gods who have pinned a little hope on you.

choices.text: Go up the star-road, and meet them

effects.log: You go up. The crowd parts, and the duel begins in a silence like a held breath.

choices.text: Decline, and watch from the second step

effects.log: You decline. The second step is, you find, a very good place to watch the future go by.

events.text: The elder gods of {ow9_order} have rallied to you one by one, and now {ow9_foe} stands alone in the cloister, with a spear of light and a very straight back. It would end quickly. It would also be remembered. The pantheon looks on, hushed, hoping for a clean ending.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} in the open, and finish it

effects.log: You meet them. The cloister watches, and it is quick, and it is cleanly done.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} a shrine and a place at your altar

effects.log: You offer terms. {ow9_foe} takes a long time to say yes, and then says it well.

events.text: With the voices behind you, the matter of {ow9_seat} is nearly settled. {ow9_foe} sends a last hymn: a duel, if you like, or terms, if you are wise. The hall of {ow9_order} is lit for either. Someone has already laid out a seat, a spear, and a cup of star-wine.

choices.text: Take the duel, and be done

effects.log: You take it. The spear is lighter than you thought, and the ending cleaner.

choices.text: Set the wine aside, and write the terms

effects.log: You set the wine aside, and write the terms. They are generous, and fair.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_seat} is yours. {ow9_old}'s lamp still burns beside it, and the first thing you do is trim it. The pantheon of {ow9_order} has begun to say your name in the tone of a house that has decided. In the corner, a very old acolyte weeps into a very large censer.

choices.text: Keep {ow9_old}'s mantle by the seat

effects.log: You keep it. The pantheon is quietly glad.

choices.text: Give the seat's first feast to every shrine

effects.log: You give the feast. Every shrine is full, and the lamps burn until dawn.

events.text: You sit in {ow9_seat} for the first time, and it is, as every seat is, a little too hard. {ow9_old} would have told you that. The elders of {ow9_order} bow in order, the youngest last. Outside, the star-road is swept, and a hundred heralds are lifting off with the news.

choices.text: Rise, and walk the domain before dusk

effects.log: You walk it. The acolytes line the path, and the old stones are warm under your feet.

choices.text: Send a hymn to {ow9_foe}, and invite them to supper

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} comes, and the supper is awkward and honest.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sits in {ow9_seat}, and you stand in the second row. It is not a disgrace, but it is a position. {ow9_old} would have said something wise. You say nothing, and bow when the others bow. The wine afterward is unusually good.

choices.text: Bow deeply, and mean none of it yet

effects.log: You bow. Meaning will come, or it will not.

choices.text: Write your faults in the Book, in a plain hand

effects.log: You write them. The list is shorter than you feared, and sharper.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_order} is {ow9_foe}'s, and the pantheon breathes out. You are left with your altar, your faith, and a long list of gods who no longer meet your eye. The Terrace of Dawn is swept clean. A single dove lands on the rail, looks at you, and leaves.

choices.text: Walk the cloister at night, alone

effects.log: You walk it. The stones are cool, and you learn the names of the lamps.

choices.text: Send {ow9_foe} a gift, and a short, honest hymn

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} sends back a gift of incense, which is a start.

events.text: {op9_holder}, who keeps {op9_post}, will swear to {op9_seat} for a price, and says so over a pot of weak tea in the corner of the hall. It is a fair price, for the kingdoms. {op9_voice} adds that {op9_n} others have already sworn, and that {op9_post} does not like to be the last.

choices.text: Pay the price, and have the oath

effects.log: The coin changes hands and the oath is made. {op9_holder} looks almost fond of the transaction.

choices.text: Decline, and say the house is not for sale

effects.log: You decline politely. {op9_post} stays its own master, which is what it hoped.

events.text: A river-barge brings a bill: the keeper of {op9_post}, {op9_holder}, would like a gift of silver before swearing to {op9_seat}. Not a bribe, the letter insists, but a fee. It is written in a very small, very expensive hand, and the seal is not the magistrate's.

choices.text: Settle the fee, and call it an oath

effects.log: The fee goes by the next barge. A week later, so does the oath.

choices.text: Send the letter back with a cup of plain tea

effects.log: The letter goes back with the tea. It is the one reply the keeper had not drafted for.

events.text: {op9_holder} sends no word, only a ledger, open on the table of {op9_post}: the cost of lamp-oil, the cost of copyists, the cost of a roof that has leaked since the last flood. The sum at the bottom is circled. {op9_voice} does not mention it. Everyone else does.

choices.text: Cover the sum, and take the oath that follows

effects.log: The roof is mended and the lamps lit. {op9_holder} swears with a hand on the new beam.

choices.text: Close the ledger, and offer a smaller kindness

effects.log: You offer a smaller kindness. It is accepted with a thin smile, and no oath.

events.text: {op9_holder} will not swear to {op9_seat} on word alone. In {op9_post}, they set out a blank page and ask you to tell it who you are in a way the school's old teachers will believe. {op9_n} others have tried. A dozen pupils have found reasons to loiter on the stair.

choices.text: Speak to the page, and make it listen

ok.log: The page seems to warm as you speak. {op9_holder} reads it twice and bows.

fail.log: The page stays cold. You said true things, but not in the right order.

choices.text: Decline the test, and say the house needs no witness

effects.log: You decline. The page is rolled up with a small, offended rustle.

events.text: In the lowest room of {op9_post}, {op9_holder} lays out a puzzle that the school has kept for generations: a map of the kingdom with one river missing. Whoever finds it, swears, say the old teachers. {op9_voice} lights the lamps, and the room smells of ink and damp wool.

choices.text: Study the map, and find the river

ok.log: You find the river under a smudge no one noticed. {op9_holder} swears, looking relieved.

fail.log: The river will not be found. You lose an afternoon, and the keeper loses patience.

choices.text: Say you came for friends, not riddles

effects.log: You say it plainly. The map is rolled up, and {op9_holder} laughs, once, shortly.

events.text: The keeper's way is a bout of arms, and {op9_holder} has chosen the training yard of {op9_post} for it. Wooden staves only, and the old forms. Behind them {op9_voice} counts a breath for each year the school has stood. Win, and the oath is yours.

choices.text: Meet the keeper in the yard

ok.log: You win with a form older than the school that {op9_holder} had thought lost. The oath is given on the spot.

fail.log: The keeper is better than the rumours. You limp out with a bruise and a polite word.

choices.text: Bow, and say friends are not made by force

effects.log: You bow. {op9_holder} bows back, in a way that is neither agreement nor offence.

events.text: {op9_holder} asks for no coin and sets no test, only a promise, spoken in {op9_post}, to be kept at a time they will name. {op9_voice} brings a cup of rice wine, and says it is a very old kind of oath, and a very dull one. {op9_n} have given it already.

choices.text: Give the promise, and raise the cup to it

effects.log: You give it, and raise the cup, and set it down full. Somewhere in the walls of {op9_post}, an old bell sounds once.

choices.text: Say you do not promise what you cannot yet see

effects.log: You say so, kindly. {op9_holder} writes something down, and does not say what.

events.text: The keeper of {op9_post} puts a folded paper on the table without a word. It says that when the day comes, you will do one thing, and does not say what. The ink is ordinary, the paper is old, and {op9_voice} cannot quite look at it.

choices.text: Sign the paper without reading it twice

effects.log: You sign. The paper is folded and put in a drawer, and the drawer is locked with a small satisfied click.

choices.text: Fold the paper back, and say you would rather know

effects.log: You fold it back. {op9_holder} takes it, smiles faintly, and puts it away unsigned.

events.text: On the bridge below {op9_post}, {op9_holder} stops you with one hand on the rail. A promise, they say, between friends of the house: that when the river-towns are in trouble, you will come. No terms, no witness but the water. It is, as such things go, a very generous kind of rope.

choices.text: Promise, and mean it

effects.log: You promise. The river is the only witness, and it is, as always, discreet.

choices.text: Say you will come when you can, and no promise more

effects.log: You say so. {op9_holder} accepts it, thoughtfully, as one accepts a smaller coin.

events.text: The promise made in {op9_post} falls due. {op9_holder} sends no messenger; they come themselves, in plain clothes, on the last ferry of the season. The thing they ask is smaller than you feared and harder than you hoped. {op9_voice} waits at the landing, pretending not to listen.

choices.text: Keep the promise, whatever it costs

effects.log: You keep it. {op9_holder} bows lower than the occasion needs.

choices.text: Break it, and send the keeper away

effects.log: You break it. The ferry leaves with a single passenger, and {op9_post} stays silent for years.

events.text: A letter in an old hand, brought to your door by a pupil of {op9_post}: it is time. The thing you promised has a date now, a place by the market bridge, and a witness. {op9_holder} has underlined the date twice. You could keep it. You could find an excellent reason not to.

choices.text: Go to the bridge on the date

effects.log: You are on the bridge at dawn. {op9_holder} is there too, and neither of you mentions how long you waited.

choices.text: Find an excellent reason not to go

effects.log: The reason is excellent. It is, nevertheless, a reason, and everyone in {op9_post} knows its shape.

events.text: The bell of {op9_post} rings three times at dusk, which only happens when a promise is called in. {op9_holder} stands at the door with {op9_voice}. Nobody speaks of the oath. They speak of the weather, and the price of lamp-oil, and when the tea is done, they look at you.

choices.text: Rise, and say that you remember

effects.log: You rise and say it. The bell rings once more, softly, and the oath is closed.

choices.text: Pour more tea, and say nothing at all

effects.log: You pour more tea. The silence is an answer, and nobody drinks.

events.text: {npc} has made a move you did not expect: a gift, in your name, to the keeper of {op9_post}, which was never yours to give. It is a trap and a kindness at once. {op9_holder} cannot accept it without owing {npc}, and cannot refuse it without offending you.

choices.text: Cover the gift, and make it truly yours

effects.log: You cover it, and the gift becomes your own. {op9_holder} holds to the oath, with a small, grim smile.

choices.text: Let the gift stand, and let the debt fall where it falls

effects.log: You let it stand. The keeper owes {npc} now, and you owe the keeper an apology.

events.text: All four posts of {op9_seat} stand sworn to you at last. Every keeper of the house answers to one name. {op9_voice} stands at the head of the steps with the four keepers, who look, for once, like four of the same family.

choices.text: Thank them, one at a time, by name

effects.log: You thank them by name. Four old heads bow. {op9_voice} wipes an eye with a sleeve.

choices.text: Say nothing, and lead them in to supper

effects.log: You lead them in. The soup is excellent, and nothing at all is signed.

events.text: The four keepers of {op9_seat} come to the same room on the same day, which has not happened in living memory. They do not speak of the oaths. They sit, and one of them pours the tea. It is, you realise, a kind of peace, and the first the house has held.

choices.text: Pour the next cup yourself

effects.log: You pour. It is a small gesture, received as a large one.

choices.text: Ask each of them for one honest complaint

effects.log: You ask. It takes the afternoon, and by the end the house is better for it.

events.text: {ow9_old} is gone, and named nobody. The seat of {ow9_seat} stands empty under its lamp, and {ow9_order} holds its breath. By evening a letter comes from {ow9_foe}, perfectly courteous, announcing a claim. The magistrates have heard already, and are, in their fashion, delighted.

choices.text: Put your own claim to the school's register

effects.log: You put it in the register. The clerk writes it down without a flicker, which is a credit to good upbringing.

choices.text: Back {ow9_foe}, and kneel first

effects.log: You kneel first. {ow9_foe} is startled, then gracious, then rather quick.

choices.text: Step aside, and let the quarrel pass

effects.log: You step aside, and watch the quarrel go by like a barge in the fog.

events.text: The lamp of {ow9_seat} burns on, though {ow9_old} will never trim it again. In the yard of {ow9_order}, pupils and teachers gather in knots. {ow9_foe} is the only one who has sent for a banner. They say it is already stitched, the way one says of a banner that is not.

choices.text: Take the lamp, and sit under it

effects.log: You take the lamp and sit. The knots in the yard turn, slowly, to watch.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} your hand, and your name

effects.log: You offer both. It is taken, with a look of cautious happiness.

choices.text: Blow out the lamp, and go home

effects.log: You blow it out and go home. The yard, the next morning, is full of other people's smoke.

events.text: No will was found. {ow9_old} left tea, a pair of worn sandals and a seat of {ow9_seat} with a hundred hands reaching for it. {ow9_foe} is first among them, with a letter and a great deal of confidence. The elders of {ow9_order} look at you, one by one, and wait.

choices.text: Say you will hold the seat, and need no leave

effects.log: You say it. Several elders discover a pressing need to be elsewhere.

choices.text: Say you will follow {ow9_foe}, with conditions

effects.log: You follow, with conditions. They are written down, and some are even kept.

choices.text: Say the seat is not yours to want

effects.log: You say so. It is the truth, or nearly, and the elders hear it as modesty.

events.text: The war for {ow9_seat} is mostly teacups. In the east wing, the gardeners of {ow9_order} have not yet declared; in the west, the copyists have. {ow9_foe} dines with the copyists every night. A voice can be won honestly, bought handsomely, or leaned on. Tonight it is the gardeners.

choices.text: Walk the east wing, and ask for each voice

effects.log: You walk, and ask. Most of them say yes, as people do to the polite.

choices.text: Send the gardeners the best from your own stores

effects.log: The gifts go out. The gardeners are moved, as gardeners are, by something that grows.

choices.text: Remind the gardeners who holds their leases

effects.log: You remind them. The gardeners promise, very quietly, and remember.

events.text: A river-barge of magistrates from the League's Wardens sits off the landing of {ow9_order}, waiting to see who rules {ow9_seat}. They are not partial. They are merely curious, which is worse. {ow9_foe} has already invited them to dinner. The question is who invites them to breakfast.

choices.text: Invite them to breakfast, and tell the plain truth

effects.log: You tell them. The magistrates eat well and write nothing, which is a compliment.

choices.text: Send a hamper of the town's best, with no note

effects.log: The hamper goes aboard. The barge, in its slow way, begins to turn.

choices.text: Mention a few things the Wardens would rather not hear

effects.log: You mention them. The barge is suddenly eager to be on its way.

events.text: The old pupils of {ow9_old} are the swing. Eleven of them live in the upper house, and each has a vote worth three. They loved their teacher in different ways, which is the trouble. {ow9_foe} has promised them a memorial. You could promise a better one, or something else.

choices.text: Sit with each of them, and speak of {ow9_old}

effects.log: You sit with each, and speak. The pupils remember who came to listen.

choices.text: Promise a memorial, and pay for the first stone

effects.log: The first stone is laid. The pupils begin, noticeably, to like you.

choices.text: Hint that the memorial will never be built at all

effects.log: You hint. They go quiet, and nod, and do not meet your eye.

events.text: Under the willows of {ow9_order}, a ring of senior teachers sip wine and weigh the claims. They want to be wooed, and not seen to be. {ow9_foe} has failed at both. It is your turn, and the teacher with the longest beard is already smiling.

choices.text: Speak to them straight, without the wine

effects.log: You speak straight. Two of the old teachers nod, slowly, like a pair of herons.

choices.text: Lay out a feast the river-towns will talk about

effects.log: The feast is talked about. The senior teachers are in a mood to be generous.

choices.text: Let them know what an open quarrel will cost them

effects.log: You let them know. They take it as a statement of fact, which it is.

events.text: A scuffle breaks out in the Long Hall, between the pupils loyal to you and the pupils loyal to {ow9_foe}. Nothing is drawn but tempers, and a stool goes through a screen of painted herons. The elders of {ow9_order} watch from the gallery, and every word you say will be repeated at supper.

choices.text: Step between them and speak to both

ok.log: You step between them and speak. The scuffle drains away, and the elders are impressed.

fail.log: You step between them and speak, and are shouted over. The elders watch your face colour.

choices.text: Let them tussle, and speak to the elders instead

effects.log: You turn your back on the fray and speak to the gallery. It is a calm, risky thing to do, and it works.

events.text: The great gate of {ow9_order} is shut by one party and opened by another, three times in one morning. A bell is rung wrongly. A banner of {ow9_foe}'s is pinned over one of yours. The Record Room is next, and whoever holds the Record, holds the argument. You have maybe ten breaths.

choices.text: Find the clause in the Record that settles it

ok.log: You find the clause, a tiny line in an old charter, and read it aloud. The hall falls quiet.

fail.log: You hunt for the clause, and the clause is not where you hoped. The hall's mood is not improved.

choices.text: Stand in the gate and hold it with your name

effects.log: You stand in the gate. Your name does the rest, and the bell is rung rightly.

events.text: Rows of lanterns are carried through the halls of {ow9_order}, each side trying to outshine the other. It is a ridiculous war and a serious one. In the seal-room, a candle has been knocked over, and a cabinet of old seals is smoking. {ow9_foe} is nowhere. The seals are everywhere.

choices.text: Take command of the room, and organise the buckets

ok.log: You organise the buckets. By the time the smoke clears, the whole hall is quietly on your side.

fail.log: You shout for buckets and nobody comes. The seals are saved by a very small cook.

choices.text: Save the seals yourself, and say nothing about it

effects.log: You save the seals yourself, quietly. The copyists see it, and the copyists remember.

events.text: The matter comes down to a bout in the training yard, as these matters do. {ow9_foe} waits at the far end, in their best coat. The old gate of {ow9_seat} is watching. Your side is thin, and the elders say little. It will be close, and the whole river will hear of it.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} in the yard

effects.log: You meet them. The dust closes round the two of you, and what follows is not for the register.

choices.text: Step aside before it begins

effects.log: You step aside. {ow9_foe} is given the seat, and the yard is swept.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sends a challenge, written on rice paper, folded into a boat. The boat is set on your desk by a pupil of {ow9_order} who is visibly terrified. The terms: a single bout, no seconds, at dawn, for {ow9_seat}. You have fewer friends than you would like.

choices.text: Fold the boat back, and accept

effects.log: You accept. The boat sails home, and the house does not sleep that night.

choices.text: Burn the boat, and concede the seat

effects.log: You burn it, and concede. The smoke goes up in a thin and very polite line.

events.text: The elders have decided that the seat of {ow9_order} goes to the winner of a bout, which is to say they have decided not to decide. {ow9_foe} has trained for a year. You were busy. The steps are lined, as for a fair, with people who have pinned a little hope on you.

choices.text: Go up the steps, and meet them

effects.log: You go up. The crowd parts, and the bout begins in a silence like a held breath.

choices.text: Decline, and watch from the second step

effects.log: You decline. The second step is, you find, a very good place to watch the future go by.

events.text: The elders of {ow9_order} have rallied to you one by one, and now {ow9_foe} stands alone in the yard, with a staff and a very straight back. It would end quickly. It would also be remembered. The river-towns look on, hushed, hoping for a clean ending.

choices.text: Meet {ow9_foe} in the open, and finish it

effects.log: You meet them. The yard watches, and it is quick, and it is cleanly done.

choices.text: Offer {ow9_foe} a hall and a place at your table

effects.log: You offer terms. {ow9_foe} takes a long time to say yes, and then says it well.

events.text: With the voices behind you, the matter of {ow9_seat} is nearly settled. {ow9_foe} sends a last message: a bout, if you like, or terms, if you are wise. The hall of {ow9_order} is lit for either. Someone has already laid out a seat, a staff, and a pot of tea.

choices.text: Take the bout, and be done

effects.log: You take it. The staff is lighter than you thought, and the ending cleaner.

choices.text: Take the tea, and write the terms

effects.log: You take the tea, and write the terms. They are generous, and fair.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_seat} is yours. {ow9_old}'s lamp still burns beside it, and the first thing you do is trim it. The house of {ow9_order} has begun to say your name in the tone of a place that has decided. In the corner, a very old cook weeps into a very large pot.

choices.text: Keep {ow9_old}'s sandals by the seat

effects.log: You keep them. The house is quietly glad.

choices.text: Give the seat's first feast to the whole town

effects.log: You give the feast. Every table is full, and the lanterns burn until dawn.

events.text: You sit in {ow9_seat} for the first time, and it is, as every seat is, a little too hard. {ow9_old} would have told you that. The elders of {ow9_order} bow in order, the youngest last. Outside, the steps are swept, and a hundred ferries are casting off with the news.

choices.text: Rise, and walk the grounds before nightfall

effects.log: You walk them. The pupils line the path, and the old stones are warm under your feet.

choices.text: Send a letter to {ow9_foe}, and invite them to supper

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} comes, and the supper is awkward and honest.

events.text: {ow9_foe} sits in {ow9_seat}, and you stand in the second row. It is not a disgrace, but it is a position. {ow9_old} would have said something wise. You say nothing, and bow when the others bow. The tea afterward is unusually good.

choices.text: Bow deeply, and mean none of it yet

effects.log: You bow. Meaning will come, or it will not.

choices.text: Write your faults down, in a plain hand

effects.log: You write them. The list is shorter than you feared, and sharper.

events.text: The seat of {ow9_order} is {ow9_foe}'s, and the house breathes out. You are left with your staff, your silver, and a long list of people who no longer meet your eye. The training yard is swept clean. A single heron lands on the wall, looks at you, and leaves.

choices.text: Walk the grounds at night, alone

effects.log: You walk them. The stones are cool, and you learn the names of the lamps.

choices.text: Send {ow9_foe} a gift, and a short, honest note

effects.log: You send it. {ow9_foe} sends back a gift of tea, which is a start.
